RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

Member: Cameron Brooks (ID W412154328)
Requested Service: Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-13
Treating Surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy) described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-13. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day window stated in that notice (deadline 2027-02-09).

**Stated reason for denial**
The notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I ask the plan to reconsider based on the complete clinical record summarized below.

**Policy identified as governing this review**
Based on my own research, MVP Health Care does not appear to maintain an in-house medical policy specifically titled "Knee Arthroscopy"; MVP's member materials state that musculoskeletal surgery reviews, including knee surgery, are managed by MVP's delegated vendor (Magellan Healthcare/NIA, now operating as Evolent). The document I was able to locate and retrieve that addresses knee arthroscopy/meniscectomy is Evolent's "Knee Arthroscopy Clinical Tip Sheet," which states that it summarizes "Guideline Evolent_CG-316." I was not able to retrieve the full text of Guideline Evolent_CG-316 itself (only this summary tip sheet), so I am quoting only the tip-sheet language below and am not attributing any language to the full guideline that I have not actually seen. I ask that MVP/its delegated reviewer identify, in its response to this appeal, the exact guideline, version, and effective date actually applied to this determination, and provide a full copy of that document, so that I may respond to its complete terms if this appeal is not resolved in my favor.

**Why the clinical record supports approval**

1. Locked-knee / displaced bucket-handle tear exception.
The retrieved tip sheet states that non-operative treatment is not required in the following circumstance: "History of acute injury/onset of symptoms with a locked knee and/or mechanical symptoms of locking; Physical examination demonstrates ANY positive meniscal findings on examination or demonstrates evidence of a locked knee (loss of terminal extension); MRI demonstrates a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus. (Does not include an extruded meniscus or flap tears)."

The MRI of 2026-07-02 documents a "displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking," and the clinical record documents that the patient "experiences locking and giving way; cannot squat or kneel; limited to level walking," with "positive provocative testing on the affected side" and range of motion limited by pain. These findings appear to place this case within the category the tip sheet describes as not requiring non-operative treatment as a prerequisite to surgery. I ask that this be specifically addressed in the reconsideration.

2. Weight-bearing X-ray / arthritis-severity requirement is satisfied or inapplicable.
The tip sheet further states: "Unless the patient has a locked knee with a displaced bucket-handle tear, weight-bearing X-rays must show no more than mild arthritis for approval of meniscus procedures. (No more than K-L 2 changes...)." The MRI report documents "articular cartilage preserved, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1," which is within the stated limit in any event, and the locked-knee/bucket-handle-tear presentation independently removes this case from the arthritis-severity limitation as described above.

3. In the alternative, if conservative treatment is deemed a prerequisite, it has been fully documented and exceeds the stated minimum duration.
The same tip sheet states that most meniscal tears "WILL require documentation of non-operative treatment as follows: Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following: Rest or activity modifications/limitations; Ice/heat; Protected weight bearing; Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol; Brace/orthosis; Physical therapy modalities; Supervised home exercise; Weight optimization; Corticosteroid injection."

The record shows conservative treatment well in excess of six weeks, using more than two of the listed modalities:
- Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion: 14 weeks (2026-04-08 through 2026-07-15), 24 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Pharmacologic treatment: NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- Corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-10, providing only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- Symptom duration of 12 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, reflecting ongoing activity modification/limitation over the same period.

This is documentation of at least three of the listed modalities (physical therapy, pharmacologic treatment, corticosteroid injection) sustained well beyond six weeks, with objectively documented failure (persistent locking, giving way, inability to squat or kneel, and only transient partial relief from injection).

4. No disqualifying comorbidities.
The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker status, none of which the retrieved tip sheet identifies as a barrier to approval.

**Requested action**
Based on the clinical record and the retrieved plan criteria above, I ask that MVP Health Care reverse the denial and approve CPT 29881 (knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy) as requested by Dr. Duval. If MVP's reviewer relies on any policy language beyond what I have quoted here, I ask that the complete text of that language, along with the guideline's title, number, and effective date, be provided to me in the appeal decision so that I have a full and fair opportunity to respond.

**Enclosures**
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-08 to 2026-07-15, 24 visits)
- Medication/treatment history documenting 8 months of NSAID use
- Corticosteroid injection record dated 2026-05-10
- MRI report dated 2026-07-02
- Clinic examination notes documenting locking, giving way, functional limitations, and provocative testing
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval [to be attached]
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office wishes to include]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the expected timeframe for a decision. If expedited review is warranted given ongoing mechanical locking, please advise how to request that. I can be reached at [patient phone number] or [patient email address]. I authorize Dr. Duval's office to submit or discuss additional clinical information on my behalf if needed [attach Authorized Representative form if applicable].

Sincerely,

Cameron Brooks
Member ID: W412154328
